observation.visible_scene: A calm coastal beach at low sun (dawn/dusk): a wide still tidal pool in the foreground mirrors a dramatic cloudy sky, a dark conifer tree line and a small house sit on the right-hand shore, and a few real rocks protrude from the shallow water at left and center. The horizon, tree line, house and rocks hold fixed positions throughout, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The cloud formations in the sky slowly drift and deform: the dense central cloud mass seen in the early frames shifts rightward and breaks apart over the sequence, opening more clear sky.
The warm orange band of light near the horizon (left of center) broadens and brightens toward the middle of the frame as the excerpt progresses.
The cloud shapes occupying the lower half of the image are reflections in the still water, not separate clouds; they change in sync with the sky above rather than moving independently.
Foreground rocks, the tree line, the house and the shoreline remain in constant positions, so the only motion is in the clouds and their reflection.
No camera pan, tilt or zoom is evident; the framing of static landmarks is unchanged from first to last frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the lighting trend corresponds to a rising or setting sun, and what the sky looks like before or after this segment.
Whether any wind-driven surface ripples exist below the time-lapse sampling rate.
The actual elapsed real-world time represented by these frames (the motion pattern is consistent with a time-lapse).
uncertain_details: Exact direction and speed of individual cloud drift; only the broad rightward/fragmenting trend is clearly supported.
Whether the horizon glow intensifies because of the sun's elevation or simply because thinning clouds reveal more light.
Whether the water is perfectly still or carries very faint motion not resolvable between frames.
